accepted.sentence: Endurance athletes often eat the ripe fruit before exercise because its digestible carbohydrates provide readily available energy.
Sliced over plain yogurt, the soft flesh adds sweetness and a tender contrast to its creamy base.
In some cuisines, the tender inner core of the pseudostem is chopped and cooked as a vegetable.
Farmers may feed surplus or damaged harvests to livestock, converting unsold produce into animal nutrition.
After harvest, chopped pseudostems can be spread over fields as mulch, returning organic matter to the soil.
In some regions, ripe slices are dipped in batter and fried into sweet fritters for dessert or snacks.
Wild, seeded fruits provide food for forest animals, which can disperse seeds through their droppings.
A naturally sweet ripe portion can serve as a quick snack between meals without preparation beyond peeling.
